final_decision.rationale: Pair-0 signal analysis (SIGNAL mode, sigma=2.59): JPEG confirmed by 0%-FP block_boundary=1.3257 (severity 1: lowest peeled residual 20.4 and dct_zero_ratio 0.561 vs target 0.5587; stronger q overshoots: sev3 bb diff 11%, base jpeg5 residual 25.0). Noise confirmed but type/shape: residual_intensity_corr 0.4867 (additive gaussian/YCrCb sims approx 0) + highlight clipping pattern (target clipped 0.0205; speckle:2 sim 0.0208) point to multiplicative speckle; equal RGB channel stds rule out YCrCb (peeled rgb_ratio 1.05); var_slope -0.03 rules out Poisson; §B IMPULSE is the documented extreme_pct false positive (signed-residual counting, extreme 62.8% >50% with sigma<5). noise_speckle:2 + compression_jpeg:1 = verify_signals MATCH (3/3) and best fingerprint across 8 signals. Blur absent: spectral_slope_ratio 0.995, FFT anisotropy 0, glass 0, gm_ratio>1 (noise-dominated), peeled residual worsened with blur (20.4 -> 22.0/26.4). Global absent: variance_ratio 0.843 / mean_shift -6.9 fully reproduced by speckle clipping (sim 0.883 / -4.9), no contrast/brightness/saturation function range matches (contrast_weaken sev1 scale 0.75 would give var 0.56; brightness darken min shift -25.5). Order fixed by generator priority: noise (priority 0) before JPEG (priority 2). Verdict UNCERTAIN per protocol: noise step can never be LIKELY (seed mismatch) and deterministic PSNR>=40 is unavailable in sigma>=2 mode.

reanalysis.summary: Re-ran run_full_analysis on all 5 support pairs (full_analysis_R1.json + full_analysis_R1_p1..p4.json) and peeled_noise_check with the R0 deterministic strip (compression_jpeg:1) on all 5 pairs. Pair0 reproduces R0 exactly (same JSON values), confirming the R1 rerun is faithful. Cross-pair signals are highly consistent: JPEG in 5/5, multiplicative noise in 5/5, no blur 5/5, no global 5/5.
verdict_vs_signal_checks: Noise verdict GAUSSIAN_YCrCb in 5/5 pairs contradicts the peeled evidence: the step2 YCrCb branch (cross_ch_corr>0.12 AND RIC>0.15) returns early, so the Gaussian/Poisson/speckle fingerprinting (intensity_var_corr) is never executed (None in all 5 pairs). R1 bypassed this branch by direct family simulations and second-order fingerprints instead of trusting the verdict label.

Blur verdict BLUR_UNLIKELY is consistent with spectral_slope_ratio 0.9696-0.9954 in 5/5 pairs (all below the 1.08 threshold and below 1.0, i.e. target is not steeper than clean). glass_score/residual_anisotropy are absent because step3 returns early before those sub-signals are computed; the blur hypothesis was therefore tested end-to-end with a blur-inclusive simulation (noise:sigma 80% mismatch) rather than relying on missing sub-signals.

Global verdict NO_GLOBAL is consistent; the p4 SATURATION_strengthen_sev4 detection (chroma_ratio 1.2423) is a noise artifact: across pairs chroma_ratio scatters 0.8901-1.2423 with no uniform step, and noise can only add chroma variance, not the x2.0 minimum saturation step.

The peeled section-B extreme_pct 57.28-64.93% IMPULSE suggestion is the documented signed-residual counting false positive (residual<=0 or >=255); impulse is independently excluded by impulse_zero_ratio 0.0746-0.1656 (an impulse sev1 would leave >85% near-zero residuals).
threshold_boundary_checks: JPEG severity boundary: block_boundary target 1.3257-1.7437 vs jpeg:1 sims 1.2196 (p0, -8%) and 1.4572 (p3, -11%); jpeg:2 sims 1.3377 (p0, +0.9%) and 1.6705 (p3, +1.9%). bb alone favors jpeg:2, but dct_zero_ratio (pair0 0.6134 vs target 0.5587, +9.8%) and noise_prior_sigma (pair0 1.85 vs 2.59, -29%) regress, and verify_signals reports noise:sigma mismatches of 27% (p0) and 67% (p3). jpeg:1 wins 3 of 5 canonical signals on both audited pairs -> severity 1 retained.

Speckle severity boundary: speckle:3 sim reproduces the clipping-derived global stats on pair0 almost exactly (mean_shift -7.01 vs -6.93; variance_ratio 0.8489 vs 0.8426; RIC 0.4921 vs 0.4804) while sev2 sim undershoots (-4.89 / 0.8828 / 0.4477). However sev3 canonically loses on the block/noise-spectrum signals (sigma 3.34 vs target 2.59, +29%; bb 1.1787, -11%; dct 0.4924, -12%) and R0 recorded WEAK on pair0 (sigma 40%, bb 11%). The global-stat advantage may be a noise-realization tail effect (Gaussian multiplicative tails drive clipping excess, which mean_shift/variance_ratio integrate). Per verify_signals protocol, sev2 stands; the sev2-vs-sev3 boundary is the main residual uncertainty of this challenge.

Noise_prior_sigma is not a monotone severity readout here: peeled residual std is 12.0-21.1 levels after jpeg:1 stripping while the wavelet sigma estimate is 1.11-3.21, i.e. JPEG q25 smooths most high-frequency noise. Sigma threshold comparisons are therefore treated as secondary to the RIC/clipping/spectral fingerprints.
second_order_stats_checks: residual_intensity_corr (RIC): target 0.2490-0.5690, positive in 5/5 pairs; speckle:2 sims 0.2329-0.5481; additive gaussian_RGB -0.03, gaussian_YCrCb 0.056, poisson:2 0.2321 (pair0) -> multiplicative speckle is the only family reproducing the intensity-dependent residual magnitude.

variance_ratio and mean_shift: target variance_ratio 0.8106-0.9872 and mean_shift -0.85..-9.07 track per-pair clipped_fraction 0.0021-0.0543; speckle:2 sim reproduces clipping (pair0 0.0208 vs 0.0205; pair2 0.0521 vs 0.0532; pair4 0.0965 vs 0.0543). No x_distortion global function has a minimum step this mild (brightness shift min 25.5 levels, darken gamma sev1 1.4, contrast_weaken_scale sev1 0.75 -> variance ratio 0.5625).

Peeled residual channel statistics: rgb_ratio 1.0279-1.0764 (<1.4) and cross_ch 0.8611-0.9420 in 5/5 pairs. Cross-channel correlation is JPEG-induced (the same pair peeled under jpeg:1 leaves it), not chroma-weighted noise; gaussian_YCrCb sim RIC 0.056 vs 0.49 also excludes it.

Section-B var_slope (-0.0748..0.1538) is computed by binning on residual intensity, not clean intensity, so it is not a valid Poisson test; the poisson hypothesis was instead tested by direct simulation (RIC 0.2321, mean_shift -2.78, variance_ratio 0.9310 vs target 0.4755/-6.93/0.8426).

decision.rationale: R0 pipeline remains the best-supported explanation after re-running the full signal analysis on all 5 support pairs and testing every plausible alternative family (poisson, jpeg severity 2, speckle severities 1/3, blur-inclusive). JPEG is confirmed 5/5 by the 0%-FP block_boundary and severity 1 is the best multi-signal compromise; noise is multiplicative in 5/5 (RIC 0.24-0.57 matched only by speckle sims), YCrCb/impulse/additive gaussian/poisson are all excluded by second-order statistics; no blur and no global step can match the signals or the function severity ranges. The control reproduces R0's support verdicts exactly (3 MATCH + 2 PARTIAL). The only open uncertainty is the speckle sev2-vs-sev3 boundary (global clipping stats favor sev3, block/noise-spectrum signals favor sev2); it does not meet the CHANGE criterion and is recorded rather than acted upon.
